original_test_intent: Read the intended BMC's Redfish AccountService, validate its account-policy controls and canonical Accounts/Roles links, and produce a credential-safe, appropriately redacted configuration snapshot without mutation.
original_method: Retain one GET to /redfish/v1/AccountService, replacing hardcoded credentials and TLS bypass with approved trust/secret delivery, secure raw retention, schema validation and policy-aware redaction.
manual_activity: The security/BMC owner approves the endpoint, least-privilege credential, certificate trust, raw-evidence access and redaction rules for account names, role links and policy values.
required_inputs: BMC endpoint bound to immutable SUT identity
Approved CA bundle or certificate pin
curl/jq and Redfish AccountService schema validator
Secure raw retention and shareable redaction policy
safety_requirements: Do not expose Authorization or passwords
Never follow this case with PATCH
agent_execution_scope: Bind HTTPS endpoint/certificate to intended BMC
Capture status, headers and raw JSON securely
Validate policy controls and Accounts/Roles links
engineer_actions: Provide expected policy values or comparison source

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The endpoint is correct, but `-k` removes server identity, `-u` risks credential exposure, and dumping full JSON without a redaction boundary can disclose account-policy/resource information; readability is not schema validation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With approved certificate trust and secret-safe least-privilege authentication, issue one bounded GET to https://<BMC>/redfish/v1/AccountService, securely retain the raw response, validate HTTP/OData/Redfish policy fields and links, then export only approved redacted evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source resource, GET intent and 15/10 timing remain; no credential, trust exception or expected policy value is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Perform a target-bound security-policy inventory read with separate secure raw retention and redacted reporting, validating protocol, schema, policy fields and resource links.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces embedded privileged access, TLS bypass and readability-only acceptance with least privilege, trust, schema and data-handling controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: ServiceRoot only links to AccountService; it does not validate policy contents. PATCH verification is deliberately excluded from this read-only case.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Policy values and account/role topology are sensitive; an intercepted endpoint can harvest credentials; vendor extensions need an approved schema/profile and redaction decision.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish client or session token is equivalent only with the same certificate binding, least privilege, secure raw/redacted split and field/link validation; TLS exceptions require explicit lab approval.
expected_evidence: Immutable SUT/BMC endpoint and certificate/trust result
Credential-provider and parser versions without secret material
HTTP status, content type and relevant headers
Access-controlled raw response hash and redacted AccountService JSON

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title, path and GET procedure consistently describe AccountService retrieval. Unsafe access, weak criteria and missing redaction are deficiencies rather than contradictory Master instructions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target resource and read operation are explicit. Trust, least-privilege access, schema, policy baseline and redaction are concrete prerequisites.

review_improvement: Makes the AccountService snapshot trusted, least-privileged, schema-aware and safe to retain and share.
independent_technical_reasoning: Unlike a generic service probe, AccountService exposes controls that govern authentication failure logging, password length and account lockout, plus links that reveal account and role topology. A full raw response may be necessary for audit but is not automatically safe for a shared test log. The review therefore separates secured raw retention from redacted evidence, binds TLS before sending credentials, and treats each policy field/link as acceptance data rather than accepting pretty JSON.
